FINDING_ID: LB_F001
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claims allocation uses LIVE fingerprints and that “every active model gets work matched to its demonstrated capability,” but the role admissibility passed into `LoadBalancer` is `self.role_assignment.role_map`, which may be stale with respect to the current active pool. `RoleAssignment.reassign()` is only called at the end of `process_round()`, not before allocation. If a model was excluded or failed after the last processed round, the next allocation can be computed using an outdated COL/PAR split from a different active set. This is distinct from the already-known “stale role_map from previous round” issue because it creates a concrete ordering bug in the public allocation path: allocation is generated before any active-set-consistent role recomputation.
PROPOSED_FIX: In `DynamicManager.get_allocation()`, recompute roles immediately for the current `failure_handler.active_models` using live fingerprints before constructing `LoadBalancer`, e.g. call `self.role_assignment.reassign(current_round, active_models=..., live_fingerprints=self._live_fingerprints)` and then pass the refreshed `role_map`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F002
SEVERITY: 0.78
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.__init__()` accepts an arbitrary `role_map` without validating that it covers exactly the models in `self.models`. Missing entries silently default to `Role.PAR` in `_admissibility_mask()`. Extra entries for absent models are ignored. In a load-balancing component where admissibility is a HARD feasibility input, this is an unsafe interface: a caller typo or stale map silently broadens executor eligibility instead of failing fast.
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate in `LoadBalancer.__init__()` that `set(role_map.keys()) == {m.model_id for m in models}` and raise `ValueError` on missing or unknown model IDs. If partial maps are intentional, require that explicitly via a separate parameter or normalization function.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F003
SEVERITY: 0.73
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: Core load-balancing dataclasses still lack invariant validation for semantically bounded fields. `Task.criticality` is documented as in `[0,1]` but not checked; `Task.flaw_class` can be negative; `ModelSpec.tau`, `L`, `c`, and `L_std` can be negative; `CapabilityFingerprint` fields documented as `[0,1]`/`ℝ≥0` are unchecked. This is not just generic validation debt: load balancing branches directly on `criticality`, divides by `L`, and uses `L_std` as a standard deviation. Invalid values can silently alter redundancy and feasibility behavior.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `__post_init__` validation to `CapabilityFingerprint`, `ModelSpec`, and `Task` enforcing documented bounds: non-negative `tau/L/c/L_std`, `criticality in [0,1]`, non-negative integer-like `flaw_class`, and fingerprint fields within declared ranges.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F004
SEVERITY: 0.69
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` returns rankings over `self.capability_scores` for all known models, including inactive/excluded ones. In this module, orderings are supposed to represent current capability orderings for role allocation, but after failures and `reassign()`, excluded models remain in the returned ordering with stale scores. That can mislead downstream consumers using `get_ordering()` to interpret or audit live role allocation.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either make `get_ordering()` accept `active_only: Optional[Set[str]]` and filter accordingly, or maintain a separate live score table updated during reassignment and expose that as the default ordering.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F005
SEVERITY: 0.71
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.assign()` and `reassign()` can select a COL role even when that role is never used by load balancing. `_admissibility_mask()` treats `COL` and `PAR` identically for all tasks, and `Task.flaw_class` is ignored. That means the module computes and updates a distinct COL capability ordering, applies hysteresis and failure-history logic to it, yet Area 2 derives no allocation consequence from COL at all. This is a correctness gap inside the analytical boundary: role allocation is operationally disconnected from task allocation, not merely “adaptive routing” in general.
PROPOSED_FIX: Either encode task classes that require/prefer COL and reflect that in `_admissibility_mask()` / scoring, or collapse COL/PAR into one executor role in Area 2 until task semantics actually differentiate them.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F006
SEVERITY: 0.64
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` uses `max(col_scores, key=lambda mid: col_scores[mid])` with no deterministic tie-breaker. Initial assignment uses `_tie_break_key()` explicitly, but reassignment does not. When two active models have equal adjusted COL scores, the winner depends on insertion order of `remaining_ids`, which is derived from a `set` (`active_models`) and is therefore non-deterministic across runs/processes.
PROPOSED_FIX: Use the same deterministic ordering as `assign()`, e.g. `max(remaining_models, key=lambda m: (col_scores[m.model_id], self._tie_break_key(m)))`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F007
SEVERITY: 0.67
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` emits `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` events and records dispatch blocks against `self.fsm.current_round`, while `process_round()` had to introduce `_process_round_count` because `fsm.current_round` is not the actual just-processed round index inside the orchestration flow. This means dispatch-health bookkeeping can attach blocks to a round index inconsistent with the rest of manager accounting, corrupting the later “blocked then succeeded” pathology detection.
PROPOSED_FIX: Use the same monotonic round counter source everywhere. Add a manager method for “current dispatch round index” based on `_process_round_count` or a dedicated dispatch counter, and use that in `check_dispatch_feasibility()`.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F008
SEVERITY: 0.62
FLAW_CLASS: 6
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36
DESCRIPTION: `Allocation.matrix` shape is documented as `(J, K)` but never validated. `Allocation` methods assume `len(task_ids) == matrix.shape[0]` and `len(model_ids) == matrix.shape[1]`. A malformed `Allocation` can therefore silently misreport assignments or raise unrelated index errors later. Because `Allocation` is the primary Area-2 result type, this is a weak interface boundary.
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `Allocation.__post_init__()` validating 2-D shape, integer/binary entries, and exact agreement with `task_ids`/`model_ids` lengths.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F009
SEVERITY: 0.59
FLAW_CLASS: 7
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` repeatedly searches `models_for_scoring` linearly via `next((m for m in models_for_scoring if m.model_id == mid), None)` for each active model. This makes reassignment O(K²) in the number of models for no reason, despite model IDs being unique and stable. The module already uses indexed maps elsewhere.
PROPOSED_FIX: Build a dict once, e.g. `model_by_id = {m.model_id: m for m in models_for_scoring}`, and use direct lookup during reassignment.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: LB_F010
SEVERITY: 0.66
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.solve()` returns `(allocation, cost, balanced)` even when `_check_feasibility()` found violations, and `cost` is computed on the infeasible matrix anyway. For a constrained allocator, reporting an objective value for an infeasible solution without surfacing feasibility in the return contract is semantically misleading: callers can rank or accept a “cost” that does not correspond to any admissible allocation.
PROPOSED_FIX: Extend the return type to include `feasible` and `violations`, or return a richer `AllocationResult` dataclass. If infeasible allocations are retained for diagnostics, mark objective as diagnostic-only or omit it from the success path.
VERIFIED: TRUE
